ACME Corp — Q4 2025 Product Planning Meeting
Date: October 14, 2025
Location: Acme HQ, Conference Room B

Attendees:
  Sarah Chen      — VP of Engineering
  Marcus Rivera   — Head of Product
  Priya Nair      — Lead Architect
  Tom Kowalski    — Engineering Manager
  Lisa Okonkwo    — QA Lead

---

AGENDA ITEM 1: Platform Database Migration

Sarah Chen opened the meeting by reviewing the current state of the PostgreSQL
to CockroachDB migration project.  The team has been evaluating three options
for the Q4 roadmap.

Marcus Rivera presented the product requirements:
  - Zero downtime during migration
  - Full ACID compliance for financial transactions
  - Horizontal scaling to support 50,000 concurrent users by Q2 2026

Priya Nair walked through the technical evaluation:

  Option A — Direct CockroachDB migration using pglogical
    Pros: lowest risk, proven tooling, no schema changes required
    Cons: 3-month timeline, specialist contractor needed

  Option B — Dual-write strategy with eventual cutover
    Pros: rollback capability at any point, can be done in-house
    Cons: increased write latency during transition, complex reconciliation

  Option C — Blue-green deployment with full snapshot restore
    Pros: fastest cutover (2-week implementation)
    Cons: brief 4-hour maintenance window required

After discussion, Tom Kowalski raised the concern that Option C requires a
maintenance window that conflicts with the Black Friday peak period.  Lisa
Okonkwo confirmed that QA cannot sign off on Option C without a full regression
suite that currently does not exist.

DECISION: The team agreed to proceed with Option B — the dual-write migration
strategy.  Sarah Chen made the final call.  The migration will begin November 3
and the cutover is targeted for December 15, 2025.

Rationale: Option B preserves rollback capability and can be executed by the
internal team without specialist contractors.  The dual-write overhead was
measured at under 12ms latency increase, which is within acceptable SLA limits.

---

AGENDA ITEM 2: Authentication Service Rewrite

Marcus Rivera presented the requirement to replace the legacy session-based
authentication with a JWT + OAuth 2.0 system.  Current pain points include:

  - Session store (Redis) has become a single point of failure (3 outages in Q3)
  - Mobile clients cannot reuse session tokens across app restarts
  - Third-party integrations require service account management

Priya Nair proposed two architectural options:

  Option A — Adopt Auth0 as managed identity provider
    Pros: fast implementation (4 weeks), no operational overhead
    Cons: vendor lock-in, $80K/year licensing cost at current user volume

  Option B — Build in-house using Keycloak (self-hosted)
    Pros: full control, GDPR compliance for EU customers, one-time setup cost
    Cons: 10-week implementation, requires dedicated DevOps effort

Sarah Chen noted that the GDPR requirement makes Option B the preferred choice
given ACME's upcoming EU market expansion in Q1 2026.

DECISION: Adopt Keycloak as the self-hosted identity provider.
Decided by: Sarah Chen (VP Engineering) with agreement from Marcus Rivera.
Target completion: January 31, 2026.
Rationale: GDPR compliance is non-negotiable for EU expansion.  The 10-week
timeline fits within the Q4–Q1 window.  Keycloak reduces long-term vendor risk
compared to Auth0.

---

AGENDA ITEM 3: API Gateway Consolidation

Tom Kowalski presented the current situation: ACME runs three separate API
gateways (Kong, AWS API Gateway, and a custom Nginx proxy) inherited from
previous acquisitions.  This creates operational complexity and inconsistent
rate-limiting policies across services.

The proposal is to consolidate onto a single gateway.

Options evaluated:
  1. AWS API Gateway — already partially in use, tight AWS integration
  2. Kong (self-hosted) — most mature feature set, plugin ecosystem
  3. Envoy with custom control plane — maximum flexibility, highest complexity

Lisa Okonkwo raised the concern that consolidation without a parallel-run period
introduces significant regression risk.  She recommended a 4-week parallel run
before decommissioning any existing gateway.

DECISION: Consolidate to Kong (self-hosted) as the unified API gateway.
Decided by: Tom Kowalski and Sarah Chen jointly.
Timeline: Parallel run begins December 1, 2025; legacy gateways decommissioned
by February 28, 2026.
Rationale: Kong's plugin ecosystem supports the rate-limiting, JWT validation,
and audit-logging requirements without custom code.  AWS API Gateway was
rejected due to cloud vendor lock-in concerns consistent with broader strategy.

---

AGENDA ITEM 4: Action Items Summary

1. Priya Nair to set up dual-write infrastructure by October 28.
2. Tom Kowalski to create Keycloak proof-of-concept environment by October 31.
3. Marcus Rivera to finalize API gateway requirements document by October 21.
4. Sarah Chen to communicate migration schedule to Customer Success team.
5. Lisa Okonkwo to draft regression test plan for all three initiatives.
